title: Driver faces upgraded charges following deadly hit-and-run crash on Ewing Drive - NewsBreak
text:
By Alicia Patton ,
1 days ago
NASHVILLE, Tenn. (WKRN) — Charges have been upgraded for a driver cited in connection with a deadly hit-and-run crash that occurred Monday evening involving a pedestrian in Davidson County, officials said.
According to the Metro Nashville Police Department, the crash took place just after 6 p.m. on Ewing Drive at Brick Church Pike.
📧 Have breaking news come to you: Subscribe to News 2 email alerts →
Authorities said 68-year-old Clifford Coleman was attempting to cross Ewing Drive in the westbound lane when he was hit by a pickup truck, which left the scene. Coleman was taken to Skyline Medical Center to be treated, but died overnight.
A witness followed the pickup truck to a home on Vista Lane and reported the incident to officers, per the MNPD.
The 66-year-old driver of a Dodge Dakota was found at the home and allegedly admitted to law enforcement that she hit Coleman.
⏩ Read today’s top stories on wkrn.com
Initially, the 66-year-old driver was issued state citations for leaving the scene of an accident and failure to file a report of an accident. However, officials said those charges will now be upgraded following Coleman’s death.
No additional details were immediately released.
